slots.dense-argument/claim/text: One observable end-to-end journey is the right first investment
slots.dense-argument/context/text: SYNTHETIC BASELINE: 18,000 cases/month • 22% manual handoffs • 14% incomplete intake • definitions and sample coverage need validation
slots.dense-argument/qualification/text: Only the four-week discovery/definition decision is requested; subsequent timing and commercial terms are not committed.
slots.dense-argument/argument-panels/understan: Replacing only the portal would leave exceptions, duplicate case state, and difficult audit reconstruction. Four teams exchange status in spreadsheets across three downstream systems, making handoffs and case history difficult to reconstruct.
The organization and operating conditions are synthetic. Fictional qualification scenario; not an actual client opportunity or West Monroe result.
Validate the assumed volumes and rates through agreed definitions and sample coverage. Produce a journey and ownership map and an interface/dependency register.
slots.dense-argument/argument-panels/prove-1/m: Use the first release to make one end-to-end journey observable and governable. Connect intake, a visible service queue, one supported integration and auditable case history; include exception and control evidence in the first proof.
slots.dense-argument/argument-panels/prove-1/b: Keep existing processing systems available during the first release. Preserve transaction ownership until an explicit migration decision. Real-time support and platform consolidation are not assumed.
slots.dense-argument/argument-panels/prove-2/e: A prioritized thin-release backlog, agreed acceptance measures, test evidence, control findings and operational runbooks. Additional journeys and integrations need separate scope decisions.
slots.dense-argument/argument-panels/decide-1/: Authorize a four-week discovery and first-release definition phase. Make authorization conditional on access readiness and agreed acceptance measures. Use discovery to confirm release scope, dependencies and the delivery sequence.
Pilot readiness requires accepted test evidence, resolved critical control findings, executable runbooks and rehearsed rollback. No fee or remaining-program date is committed.
slots.dense-argument/argument-panels/decide-2/: Proceed, hold or adjust at explicit steering gates. Validated baseline and pilot data must support expansion; weak evidence or changed conditions require a scope adjustment.
slots.slide/takeaway: A governed first journey makes the initial investment reviewable while preserving existing processing systems.
